haiku-low.q1: They see the generic message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and nothing is sent.
haiku-low.q2: The request is refused with the generic message. Nothing is written or sent, and earlier unused links stay valid.
haiku-low.q3: It works for 30 minutes after creation. A completed reset, a newer link superseding it, or a dropped email send ends it sooner.
haiku-low.q4: The link stays valid and unchanged. The form shows the error with the same token, so the user can retry until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: No devices stay logged in; all sessions, including this one, are deleted. The user is redirected to /login and must log in again.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then drops the job, sets invalidated_at, emits a metric and alerts. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is generated per request and sent only in the email link and email job. Only its SHA-256 hash is stored.
haiku-low.q8: It hashes the token with SHA-256, finds the row by token_hash, then checks used_at, invalidated_at and expires_at > now().
haiku-low.q9: A count of the user's password_reset_tokens rows with created_at in the last rolling hour. Old rows drop out of the window as time passes.
haiku-low.q10: Inside the same transaction, before the new row is inserted, all earlier unused, non-invalidated links get invalidated_at set to now().
haiku-low.q11: One transaction sets the new password hash, marks the link used, and deletes all the user's sessions. The confirmation email is queued after COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: Both requests lock the user row, then the token row. The second waits, then sees used_at set and gets the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic 200 message: "If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link." Nothing is written and nothing is sent.
sonnet.q2: It is refused (3 links already issued in the rolling hour). They get the same generic 200 message. Nothing is written or sent, and earlier unused links stay valid.
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes (expires_at = now + 30 min). It can end sooner if it is used for a reset, invalidated by a newer link request, or invalidated when the worker drops the email job after failed sends.
sonnet.q4: Untouched and still valid. The transaction rolls back, the form is shown again with the error and the same t, and the user can retry until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None. All the user's sessions rows are deleted, including the current device, and the session cookie is cleared. The user is redirected (302) to /login and logs in again with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs and drops the job. On drop it sets invalidated_at on the row (token_id), emits a metric and raises an alert. The row still counts toward the limit. The user is not told and still sees the generic message.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is generated before the transaction. After commit it is put in the email job {to, token_id, raw token} on the email queue. The worker sends the job through the mail provider, and the raw token goes into the emailed link.
sonnet.q8: It hashes t with SHA-256 and looks up the row in password_reset_tokens by token_hash. The link is good if the row is found, used_at IS NULL, invalidated_at IS NULL and expires_at > now. Otherwise it shows the expired page.
sonnet.q9: It is not stored as a counter. It is counted from password_reset_tokens rows for the user with created_at within the last rolling hour (used and invalidated rows included). Old requests drop out as created_at ages past 1 hour. A periodic cleanup also deletes rows older than 1 hour.
sonnet.q10: In the forgot-request transaction, after the lock and the count check passes (under the limit) and before inserting the new row, all the account's earlier unused, not-yet-invalidated links get invalidated_at = now(). A refused over-limit request invalidates nothing.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction, users.password_hash is updated (argon2id), the token's used_at is set, and all of the user's sessions rows are deleted. The "password was changed" email is queued after COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: Row locks. The submit locks the user row, then the token row (FOR UPDATE). The second submit waits on the token lock. After the first commits, the second sees used_at set and gets the expired page. So exactly one used_at is set and one password change happens.
